title: bug: a live release.decide outruns the browser's 15s transport abort, so the operator never sees the PR link
description:
Filed from task-817d893fa1254a4d82d2888af1f87a47 step 4 (the Gate 3 LIVE drive). MEASURED, not inferred: real pull request https://github.com/yaront1111/Moe-NG/pull/32 was opened by the product on 2026-09-08T17:04:12Z and the browser session that ordered it never rendered the link.

REPRO (tests/e2e/control-room/release-approval-live.spec.ts, MOE_LIVE_RELEASE_PR=1 against a real GitHub remote): arm + confirm the Release card. `release.decide` runs publishOnce, then `gh pr create`, then a `gh pr view` re-read (release-decide-service.ts:193-206, release-pr-port.ts:189-196) and takes tens of seconds against a real remote. The browser command transport aborts at 15s (packages/control-room-client/src/client-transport.ts:118 DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS, no requestTimeoutMs supplied by the release path). LiveGoalRelease's post-submit refresh() (live-goal-release.tsx:38) then fires into the still-busy daemon and the read aborts too (live-effect-read.ts:70, AbortSignal.timeout(15_000)), so useEffectRead settles on ERROR and renders cr.release.read-refusal - "The release evidence could not be read right now." - which it never retries out of.

NET EFFECT: the command IS delivered, the PR IS opened and the RELEASED receipt IS recorded, but the operator's card ends on an error note. Only a remount/reload surfaces the link. The Gate 3 promise "the PR link renders after a RELEASED receipt" holds only for a fast (faked) gh.

NOT this row's to fix: task-817d893f proves Gate 3, it does not rebuild it (its task rail 1), and the timeout lives in the shared command transport, not in the release card. The live spec asserts the true behaviour (receipt polled off /release/read, then the goal re-opened) and carries this defect in a comment.

SUGGESTED SHAPE (not a plan): either raise requestTimeoutMs for the long-running command kinds, or make release.decide return promptly and let the card poll the receipt - and give LiveGoalRelease a retry rather than a terminal ERROR state.
definitionOfDone: A browser session that confirms a release against a slow (real) gh either keeps waiting for the daemon's answer or recovers on its own: the PR link appears in the SAME session without a manual reload. Asserted by a test that makes the decide take longer than the transport bound.
The refusal path is unchanged: a genuinely refused release still renders its code VERBATIM with its layer, and a transport abort is still distinguishable from a daemon refusal by code.

implementationPlan.description:
SETTLE THE MECHANISM — THE FILING'S KEY CLAIM IS CONTRADICTED BY THE SOURCE. NO EDITS. Do this before writing a line; the rest of the plan is written to survive either answer, but the record needs the truth.

THE DISCREPANCY. The description and the live spec's comment (release-approval-live.spec.ts:315) both say the card lands on `cr.release.read-refusal`, "which `useEffectRead` never retries out of". Read apps/control-room/src/v2/components/use-effect-read.ts and check that against the code:
- `:19` installs `setInterval(refresh, pollMs)` with `pollMs = 5_000` — a 5-SECOND POLL, not a one-shot.
- the failure path is `.catch(() => failure).then((value) => { setFrame({ read, value }); busy = false; ... })` (:12-16), so an aborted read STORES the failure value AND clears `busy`. Nothing latches.
- the effect's deps are `[read, failure, pollMs]`; in live-goal-release.tsx `read` is a `useMemo` on `[setup, goalId]` and `failure` is a module constant, so the effect is not torn down between polls.
On the source, the hook RETRIES every 5s. Either the claim is wrong, or something else latches.

SETTLE IT WITH A MEASUREMENT, not by re-reading. The cheapest discriminator is a component-level test, not the live lane: render `LiveGoalRelease` with a reader that fails the first N calls and then returns a PRESENT receipt, advance timers past 5_000, and see whether the card leaves `cr.release.read-refusal` on its own. `use-effect-read.test.tsx` already exists next to the hook — read it first for the fake-timer idiom this codebase uses.

ALSO CHECK THE OTHER LATCH CANDIDATE, because it produces the same operator-visible symptom by a different route: live-goal-release.tsx:44 computes `offered = releaseOffer(frame, goalId) !== null` from the BOARD frame, and :46-50 returns the error note only when `offered`, else `null`. After a RELEASED receipt the daemon stops offering `release.decide`, so the card can also DISAPPEAR rather than show the link. Record which of the two the operator actually saw.

RECORD, verbatim, in the step note: whether the 5s poll fires; whether the card recovers on its own and after how long; and which state it ends in. If the poll DOES work, say so plainly — the filing's parenthetical is then wrong and the defect is narrower (a card that reports a FAILURE while the command is still in flight), which is still a real defect and still what DoD 1 asks you to fix. Do not soften the record to match the filing.
implementationPlan.note:
SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY RE-READING. The filing's parenthetical is WRONG: `useEffectRead` DOES retry, the 5s poll DOES fire, and the card DOES recover on its own. Recorded verbatim rather than softened to match the filing.

INSTRUMENT: a throwaway component probe `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.probe.test.tsx` (created, run, DELETED in this step; `git status --porcelain -- apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/` is empty). It rendered the real `LiveGoalRelease` over a fake `LiveSetup` (the `incident-dismiss.test.tsx:47-57` idiom) with `vi.stubGlobal("fetch", ...)` answering `/release/read`, vitest fake timers, and `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync`. Console output is swallowed by this runner, so the transcript was emitted by throwing it from `afterAll`. Full transcript, verbatim from the run:

  TRANSCRIPT || PROBE A t=0     reads=1 refusal=true  link=false root=false
             || PROBE A t=5000  reads=2 refusal=false link=true  root=true
             || PROBE A t=15000 reads=4 refusal=false link=true  root=true
             || PROBE B t=0     reads=1 refusal=false link=false root=false
             || PROBE B t=20000 reads=5 refusal=false link=true  root=true
             || PROBE C t=20000 reads=5 refusal=true  link=false root=false
  Test Files 1 failed (1) / Tests 3 passed (3)   [the "failed" is the afterAll transcript throw]

ANSWERS TO THE THREE QUESTIONS THE STEP ASKS:
1. DOES THE 5s POLL FIRE? YES. Probe C keeps every read failing for 20s and the read count reaches 5 = 1 initial + 4 polls at 5s intervals. Nothing latches, nothing tears the effect down. The source at use-effect-read.ts:12-19 was right and the filing's "which useEffectRead never retries out of" is false.
2. DOES THE CARD RECOVER ON ITS OWN, AND AFTER HOW LONG? YES, at the FIRST poll after the read starts answering. Probe A: `cr.release.read-refusal` at t=0 with reads=1; at t=5000 (reads=2) the refusal is gone and `cr.release.link` is rendered, same mount, no remount, no reload.
3. WHICH STATE DOES IT END IN? PRESENT with the link, in every arm where the read eventually answers (A and B). It ends on the refusal only while the read is STILL failing (C).

THE OTHER LATCH CANDIDATE, ALSO MEASURED (probe B, `offers: []` = the post-RELEASED frame after the daemon withdraws `release.decide`): the card renders NOTHING AT ALL during the failing read — refusal=false link=false root=false — because live-goal-release.tsx:46-50 returns null when `!offered`. So the two routes produce two different operator-visible symptoms: with the offer still standing the operator sees the false error note; with the offer withdrawn the card VANISHES. Both resolve to the link once a read answers.

WHAT THE OPERATOR ACTUALLY SAW IN THE LIVE DRIVE is the first: the live spec's browser session had the offer standing when it confirmed, and `release-approval-live.spec.ts:315` records `cr.release.read-refusal`. Note the live geometry makes the false window far wider than the 5s this probe shows: each poll's own read has its own 15s abort (live-effect-read.ts:70), and the daemon is busy in `gh pr create` + `gh pr view` for tens of seconds, so EVERY poll during that window aborts too. The operator reads "The release evidence could not be read right now." for as long as the daemon is opening the pull request.

SO THE DEFECT IS NARROWER THAN FILED, AND STILL REAL, AND STILL EXACTLY WHAT DoD 1 ASKS FOR: the card reports a FAILURE about a command that is succeeding. The fix in step 3 is unchanged by this measurement — hold the outstanding-submit state in the port wrapper so a failed read reads as PENDING, not failed — and step 3's conditional clause ("IF AND ONLY IF the 5s poll does not fire, also fix use-effect-read.ts") is NOT triggered: the poll fires, so use-effect-read.ts is NOT touched.

SHARED CHECKOUT: peer dirt noted, not touched — .moe/** board state, .codex/.grok config, apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts, packages/store/**, docs/agent-stack-runbook.md, plus untracked tests/e2e/foundation/** and apps/daemon/src/preview/preview-goal-landing.test.ts. None reverted, stashed or committed.

FILES: none created or modified that survive this step (the probe was deleted).

implementationPlan.description:
THE FIX — A CLIENT-SIDE TIMEOUT IS NOT EVIDENCE THE COMMAND DID NOT HAPPEN.

That sentence is the whole row. The daemon received `release.decide`, opened PR #32 and recorded a RELEASED receipt; the browser stopped waiting and then told the operator the evidence "could not be read right now". The card reported a failure about work that was succeeding.

IN apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.tsx, hold the fact that a submit is OUTSTANDING and let it govern the ERROR branch at :46-50. While a submit has been sent and has not come back with a DAEMON answer, a failed read is PENDING, not failed: keep the card in a waiting state (or keep the last good evidence on screen) and let the existing poll deliver the receipt. The port wrapper at :34-43 already intercepts every submit — that is the seam; do not add a second decision path, and do not reshape `createReleasePort`.

THE STATE MUST CLEAR. Whatever marks the submit outstanding has to be released when the daemon answers, when a read finally succeeds, and on unmount — a card stuck in "waiting" forever is the same defect wearing a friendlier word. Say in a comment what clears it.

IF, AND ONLY IF, STEP 1 MEASURED THAT THE 5s POLL DOES NOT FIRE, also fix apps/control-room/src/v2/components/use-effect-read.ts — and then say exactly what latched, because the source at :12-19 says it should not. Do not touch that hook on suspicion: it backs several cards, and a change there is a change to all of them.

DO NOT RAISE `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` (client-transport.ts:118) AND DO NOT THREAD A LONGER `requestTimeoutMs` FOR THIS KIND. The description offers it as one shape; it is the wrong one here. That constant is the shared bound for EVERY command kind in the control room, a real `gh pr create` plus `gh pr view` has no bound the browser can know in advance, and a number picked to cover the observed run re-arms for the first slower remote — while the operator stares at a spinner with no evidence either way. Recovering is right; guessing a bigger number is not. If you conclude otherwise, stop and say so with the measurement rather than changing it.

Re-run step 2's arm and confirm it goes GREEN.
implementationPlan.note:
THE FIX LANDED IN THE SEAM THE PLAN NAMED. apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.tsx only — 103 lines, well under the 250 target. `createReleasePort` is unreshaped, no second decision path, and `use-effect-read.ts` is UNTOUCHED.

STEP 3's CONDITIONAL CLAUSE IS NOT TRIGGERED. Step 1 measured the 5s poll firing (probe C: 5 reads in 20s = 1 initial + 4 polls) and the card recovering on its own at the first poll after the read answers. So the "IF AND ONLY IF the poll does not fire" branch does not apply and the hook that backs several other cards was not modified.

WHAT CHANGED, mechanically:
1. `waiting` (useState) — true from the moment a decide is sent until the daemon has said something about it. The port wrapper (already the interceptor for every submit) sets it before `wire.submit` and clears it on the answer.
2. `held` (useState) — the last evidence a read actually returned, so the window shows real numbers rather than an empty card.
3. The ERROR/REFUSED branch: `waiting ? <GoalRelease evidence={held} .../> : offered ? <OutcomeNote .../> : null`. The un-waiting behaviour is byte-for-byte what it was.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE PRODUCTION TYPE SYSTEM, NOT A GUESS. `spendOffer` (offer-wire.ts:109) returns `{ code: sent.code, layer: TRANSPORT_LAYER, ok: false }` for, and ONLY for, `!sent.delivered`; build failures answer at BUILD_LAYER and daemon refusals at the daemon's own layer or "DAEMON". So the clear condition is `result.ok || result.layer !== CONTROL_ROOM_TRANSPORT_LAYER` — the constant IMPORTED from `@moe/control-room-client` (its barrel index.ts:4 value-exports it; apps/control-room/package.json:12 already declares `@moe/control-room-client: workspace:*`, so no new dependency edge).

WHAT CLEARS THE STATE — stated in the file's own comment at the `waiting` declaration, four ways, because a card stuck in "waiting" forever is the same defect wearing a friendlier word:
- a DELIVERED answer of any kind, refusal included (the daemon spoke, so the fate is known);
- a submit that threw (the `catch` arm);
- the next read that succeeds (the `useEffect` on `outcome`);
- unmount — state dies with the component, and a `live` ref stops a late settle from writing to a card that is gone.

`held` IS NON-NULL IN EVERY REACHABLE WAITING CASE, and the file says so: `canApprove` (goal-release.tsx:91) requires `sha !== null`, which only a successful read supplies, so a decide cannot be confirmed before the card has held evidence.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, as the step directs: `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` (client-transport.ts:118) is unchanged and no `requestTimeoutMs` was threaded. Two measured reasons beyond the shared-bound objection: that constant is the round-trip bound for EVERY control-room command kind, and it would not even reach the read path — the read is a bare `fetch` in `readEffect` with `AbortSignal.timeout(15_000)` HARD-CODED at live-effect-read.ts:70, taking no option. A number chosen to cover the observed run re-arms for the first slower remote.

implementationPlan.description:
THE REFUSAL PATH IS UNCHANGED, AND THAT IS A SEPARATE ARM (DoD 2). Both clauses, in the same new test file.

(a) A GENUINE DAEMON REFUSAL STILL RENDERS ITS CODE VERBATIM WITH ITS LAYER. Drive a submit that comes back DELIVERED with a refusal, and assert the rendered `CODE @ LAYER` text — `OutcomeNote` prints exactly that inside its Details block (outcome-note.tsx:22). Use the release vocabulary's real code, `RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE`, not an invented one, and assert the LITERAL string. This is the arm that stops step 3's "treat a failure as pending" from swallowing a real refusal — which is the one way this fix could do harm, so write it as though that is what you are hunting.

(b) A TRANSPORT ABORT IS STILL DISTINGUISHABLE FROM A DAEMON REFUSAL BY CODE. Assert the two paths reach DIFFERENT codes, and assert them by their literal values — not merely that both are non-empty, and not by asserting only that a note rendered. Project rail 1: a test that asserts only "it refused" is one added layer away from vacuous. The discriminator already exists in the type system — `TransportRefused` carries `delivered: false` and a transport-layer code, a daemon answer carries the engine's own code and layer — so assert the layer too, and pin WHICH layer answered.

A note on framing worth putting in the file's header comment: the fix in step 3 does not make a transport abort mean "success". It makes it mean "unknown, still waiting", which is what it has always actually meant. The refusal vocabulary is untouched, and these two arms are the proof.
implementationPlan.note:
DoD 2 ARMED, THREE ARMS, same file. `npx vitest run src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx` (cwd apps/control-room) -> exit 0, `Test Files  1 passed (1)` / `Tests  4 passed (4)`.

2(a) "renders a DELIVERED RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE verbatim, with its layer, and keeps it". The daemon answers DELIVERED with the release vocabulary's REAL code and the layer `RELEASE_DECIDE_CODE_LAYER_MAP` maps it to (release-decide-contracts.test.ts:46 pins it to GOAL_PREREQUISITE_LAYER; the browser sees it as `DAEMON_PREREQUISITE`, matching offer-wire.test.ts:46-48 and goal-release.test.tsx:279). Asserted by EXACT EQUALITY on the `<code>` element `OutcomeNote` prints -- `toBe("RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE @ DAEMON_PREREQUISITE")`, not `toContain`, not "a note rendered", not "it refused". The daemon's `detail` is asserted too (`toBe(EVIDENCE_DETAIL)`), because that is what tells the operator WHICH criteria to chase. Then 20s of poll cycles pass and the same exact string is re-asserted, so a later re-render cannot quietly replace a refusal nobody has read yet.

2(a) SCOPE HALF -- "stops waiting once the daemon has ANSWERED, so a later failed read is reported again". This is the arm that stops the fix from blindfolding the read path for the rest of the card's life: a DELIVERED refusal ENDS the wait, and the next failing read is once again reported as `cr.release.read-refusal`, asserted by exact equality on `TRANSPORT_REQUEST_FAILED @ CONTROL_ROOM_RELEASE_READ`. The read is flipped to aborting FROM INSIDE `sendCommand` -- the instant the daemon answers -- because that is the only window in which the guard's scope is observable; a successful read would clear the wait by itself and the arm would pass whatever the guard did. This is the arm step 5 drill (ii) re-reds.

2(b) "keeps a transport abort and a daemon refusal at different codes AND different layers". Drives both paths in one arm and pins BOTH literals by exact equality -- `RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE @ DAEMON_PREREQUISITE` vs `TRANSPORT_REQUEST_FAILED @ CONTROL_ROOM_TRANSPORT` -- then asserts they differ AND that neither borrows the other's vocabulary in EITHER DIRECTION (four `not.toContain`, code and layer, both ways). The layer is the point, not decoration: `CONTROL_ROOM_TRANSPORT` is the BROWSER saying it never got an answer; `DAEMON_PREREQUISITE` is the DAEMON saying it looked at the evidence and said no. An operator who cannot tell those apart cannot know whether to fix a criterion or simply wait.

NOT VACUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION -- every one of the three arms asserts `wire.sends() === 1`. That is the positive control the incident-dismiss.test.tsx:40-46 comment documents: with an empty command roster `spendOffer` refuses OFFER_KIND_UNBUILDABLE at a NEARER layer and never reaches the transport, and an arm without this check would be asserting about a refusal the daemon never sent. Here the transport is provably reached exactly once, so the rendered code demonstrably came from where the arm claims.

FRAMING, in the file's header comment as the step asks: the fix does not make a transport abort mean "success" -- it makes it mean "unknown, still waiting", which is what an undelivered round trip has always meant, and `client-transport.ts:103-106` says so in its own words. The refusal vocabulary is untouched; these arms are the proof.

Production source unchanged in this step. Peer dirt noted and untouched.

ARCHITECT architect-5385678f 2026-09-08 — PLANNED (5 steps / 2 files, 1 new). One correction to the filing that the worker must settle FIRST, and it changes what gets fixed.

THE "NEVER RETRIES" CLAIM IS CONTRADICTED BY THE SOURCE. Both the description and release-approval-live.spec.ts:315 say the card lands on `cr.release.read-refusal`, "which `useEffectRead` never retries out of". Read apps/control-room/src/v2/components/use-effect-read.ts:
- `:19` installs `setInterval(refresh, pollMs)` with `pollMs = 5_000` — a five-second POLL, not a one-shot read.
- `:12-16` the failure path is `.catch(() => failure).then((value) => { setFrame({ read, value }); busy = false; … })` — an aborted read STORES the failure value AND clears `busy`. Nothing latches.
- deps are `[read, failure, pollMs]`; in live-goal-release.tsx `read` is a `useMemo` over `[setup, goalId]` (:32) and `failure` is a module constant (:23-25), so the effect is never torn down between polls.
On the source, the hook retries every 5s. Either the parenthetical is wrong, or something else latches. I did not run the live lane, so I am not overturning a field observation from a plan seat — step 1 settles it with a component-level test and fake timers, and is told to record the answer plainly even if it contradicts the filing.

THE OTHER LATCH CANDIDATE, same operator-visible symptom, different route: live-goal-release.tsx:44 computes `offered = releaseOffer(frame, goalId) !== null` from the BOARD frame, and :46-50 renders the error note ONLY when `offered`, else returns `null`. After a RELEASED receipt the daemon stops offering `release.decide` (parent row's DoD 3), so the card can also VANISH rather than show the link. Step 1 records which was actually seen.

WHY THE PLAN IS STILL DECISIVE. Under BOTH readings the same defect is present and the same fix answers it: **the card reports a FAILURE about a command that is succeeding.** "The release evidence could not be read right now" is on screen while the daemon is opening the pull request. A client-side timeout is not evidence the command did not happen — client-transport.ts:103-106 says `delivered` separates "a daemon that refused" from "a daemon that never answered", and a 15s abort is the second, which means UNKNOWN, not failed. So the fix holds an outstanding-submit state in the port wrapper at :34-43 (a seam that already intercepts every submit) and lets a failed read read as PENDING while one is in flight; the existing poll then delivers the receipt in the same session.

REJECTED — RAISING THE TIMEOUT, which the description offers first. Three reasons: (1) `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` (client-transport.ts:118) is the shared bound for EVERY command kind in the control room; (2) a real `gh pr create` plus `gh pr view` has no upper bound the browser can know in advance, so a number picked to cover the observed run re-arms for the first slower remote — the same "bound calibrated against a moving quantity" this board has hit twice this week (see task-0bd37766 and task-893389ae); (3) IT WOULD NOT EVEN REACH THE READ PATH. The two 15s bounds are in different transports: the command path is `ControlRoomTransport`, but the read is a bare `fetch` in `readEffect` with `AbortSignal.timeout(15_000)` HARD-CODED at live-effect-read.ts:70 and no option to supply. "Pass requestTimeoutMs on the release path" fixes half the problem by construction.

REJECTED — making `release.decide` return promptly and polling. Better long-run architecture, but the decide's answer currently IS the receipt; making it async is a wire-semantics change with a new in-flight state and every consumer updated. That is several rows, and this is a bug fix on the operator's side.

REJECTED — asserting it through the live browser lane. The live drive already opened a real PR (#32); re-running it opens another every suite run. DoD 1's clause "a test that makes the decide take longer than the transport bound" is satisfiable deterministically with fake timers at component level.

THE FIX'S OWN FAILURE MODE, which DoD 2 exists to catch and which step 5's second drill hunts: treating a failed read as "pending" is right for a transport abort and WRONG for a daemon that answered with a refusal. Step 4(a) asserts a delivered `RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE` still renders VERBATIM with its layer; drill (ii) makes the guard swallow a delivered refusal and requires that arm to go RED. The framing to keep: this does not make a transport abort mean "success" — it makes it mean "unknown, still waiting", which is what it always actually meant.

ADVERSARIAL PASS (step 5), the four questions in the order the plan asks them. Measured against source, not reasoned from the design.

Q1. THE OPERATOR CONFIRMS TWICE WHILE A SUBMIT IS OUTSTANDING. Yes, a second decide CAN leave the browser, and my fix makes it EASIER to issue than before -- that is the one honest regression surface here and I am naming it rather than burying it. Pre-fix the failing read REPLACED the whole card with the error note, so the button was gone; post-fix the card stays, so the button is visible. `busy` (goal-release.tsx:80,98,101) disables it only until the submit SETTLES, and a transport abort settles at 15s while the daemon may still be running `gh`.

WHAT STOPS IT IS THE DAEMON, at three layers, all read from release-decide-command.ts:
- :176-179 `store.getCommandDecision(key)` keyed on {commandId, principalId, projectId}. The browser spends the daemon's offer VERBATIM (release-port.ts:27-31), so a second confirm on the SAME offer row carries the SAME commandId and REPLAYS the first decision (`disposition: "REPLAYED"`). No second pull request.
- :181-187 a pending intent under INTENT_PRINCIPAL refuses `RELEASE_COMMAND_IN_PROGRESS` (409) -- exactly the "confirm again while the first is still running" case -- and :190 `hasPendingRelease` refuses the same code for any other in-flight release on the target.
- :189 `EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT` (409) once the target aggregate's version has moved, which the first decide does at :197.
All three are DELIVERED refusals, so `waiting` clears on them (the guard is scoped to `delivered:false`) and the operator reads the daemon's own code at its own layer. Bounded, fenced, disclosed -- no in-row change.

Q2. UNMOUNT MID-FLIGHT. The `live` ref is set false by the effect cleanup and every `setWaiting` in the submit path is guarded by it, so no state write lands on a gone component. The `refresh()` calls are inert after unmount too: `useEffectRead` resets `tick.current` to a no-op in its own cleanup (use-effect-read.ts:20). Nothing leaks and nothing warns.

Q3. THE DAEMON NEVER ANSWERS AT ALL. `waiting` stays true and every read keeps failing, so the card holds `held` evidence indefinitely. It is NOT a silent spinner: `cr.release.answer` carries `TRANSPORT_REQUEST_FAILED @ CONTROL_ROOM_TRANSPORT` with "That didn't go through.", which is an ACCURATE statement about the round trip. Better than what it replaced -- the old state made a FALSE claim about the evidence read while the command was succeeding. The residual gap, named honestly: the held evidence is no longer labelled as stale, so a long outage shows numbers measured minutes ago with no "this is old" marker. That is a legibility follow-up, not a false claim, and it is smaller than the defect it replaces.

Q4. IS THERE STILL A STATE WHERE THE PR LINK EXISTS IN A DURABLE RECEIPT AND THE SESSION NEVER SHOWS IT? Yes, three, and none is closable from the browser:
(a) reads fail FOREVER (daemon down). The receipt exists, this session never renders it. The operator sees the transport code instead of a false claim, and any later successful poll delivers it.
(b) the operator navigates away before a read succeeds. Covered by remount -- release-approval-live.spec.ts:320-327 asserts re-opening the goal shows the link.
(c) MEASURED in step 1 probe B and NOT changed by this row: with the offer withdrawn (post-RELEASED) and `waiting` false, a failing read renders the card as NOTHING AT ALL (live-goal-release.tsx returns null when `!offered`), so the link is absent with no error either. Pre-existing, and defensible -- there is nothing to act on -- but it is a state where the receipt exists and the session shows nothing, so it belongs in the record rather than in a claim of completeness.

INPUTS/CONCURRENCY/EXIT-PATH sweep, nothing further found: no new IO, no shared mutable state, no subprocess, no user-supplied string reaches a sink. `held` starts null and the ERROR branch tolerates null (GoalRelease already renders offer-only). Both `setWaiting` clears sit on BOTH exit paths of the submit (then and catch).
